unit: R-CLIENT / W1-4d re-review round 1: the fixer's uncommitted pass on top of wip 26b6b100 (base 1c6f6796), branch retro/w1-4-client-logout, worktree C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-r-client

defects.location: SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts refreshSession(): `const refreshToken = await SecureStore.getItemAsync(REFRESH_TOKEN_KEY);` runs BEFORE `const epochAtRequest = sessionEpoch;`. The new handoff fill `if (h.epoch === epochAtRequest) h.pair = pair;` relies on that value.
defects.claim: The ADV-A1 fix keys the handoff on epochAtRequest. That value is captured after the refresh-token read, so a read that straddles logout #1 still lets user A's refresh fill user B's logout. The schedule: A's refresh starts; its SecureStore read of RT1 stays pending past logout #1, which times out at 5 s, POSTs and runs its final clearSession (epoch 3); the read then resolves, so epochAtRequest = 3 and RT1 goes on the wire; login(B) does not bump the epoch; B's logout registers {epoch: 3}, waits on A's in-flight refresh, and A's refresh lands and fills it. I reproduced this with a scratch jest test (deleted afterwards) through the real api.ts, authService.ts and login(), holding only the first refresh-token read. HEAD result: logouts=[[A1,{refresh_token:RT1}],[A-rotated,{refresh_token:rt2-rotated-4c1d}]]. The same test on BASE 1c6f6796 sources gives [[A1,..],[B,{refresh_token:rtB-user-b-7777}]]. So within this window HEAD regresses against base. A sibling schedule is pre-existing on both base and HEAD: A's refresh lands after login(B) but before B's logout. The epoch still matches, so A's rotated tokens overwrite B's stored session (storedBeforeL2=A-rotated in both runs). The fixer's residual_risk mentions this window. It says the read must outlast 'a whole logout plus login', but measured it only needs to outlast logout #1; the network refresh then has to stay open across login(B) and B's logout tap.
defects.why_it_matters: This is the same failure as ADV-A1: B's session is not revoked upstream, and B's logout carries A's credentials. It is reachable only if a single keystore read stalls for more than 5 s while logout's own keystore reads still complete, which is unlikely if the native store serialises operations. That is why it is minor rather than major. The fix is one line and in scope: capture epochAtRequest before the SecureStore read. That also narrows the pre-existing session-swap sibling. If it is left as is, the PR text should state the window accurately.

defects.location: SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts refreshSession() handoff fill: the `&& response.data.session?.access_token` term of `if (response.data?.success && response.data.session?.access_token) {`
defects.claim: Nothing pins the access_token term of the fill guard. Mutant A16 drops it and survives all 103 tests in the 7 auth suites. Measured through the real functions: an in-flight refresh that returns 200 {success:true, session:{}} during logout makes the mutant hand off {access: undefined}. logout then takes the handoff branch with token=undefined and sends NO logout POST at all (scratch run: logouts=[] under the mutant, versus one POST with the stored AT1/RT1 on the real code).
defects.why_it_matters: The code is correct today, but a refactor that simplifies the guard would silently drop the logout POST, and with it upstream revocation, on a malformed-200 refresh. That is the property this unit exists to protect.

tests_that_prove_nothing: No test covers an epoch-guarded refresh that returns 200 {success:true} with a session that has no access_token. Mutant A16 (the `session?.access_token` term dropped from the handoff fill guard) survives all 103 tests across w1-4d, w1-4, a3, api.refreshInterceptor, api.refreshMutex, api.refreshMutex.branches and authService.m18. Under that mutant, logout sends no POST.

The ADV-A1 pin covers only a refresh whose SecureStore read finished before logout #1. No test covers the read-straddle schedule, where the read resolves after logout #1 and epochAtRequest therefore equals the later logout's pre-bump epoch. Moving the epoch capture to before the read, or leaving it where it is, keeps all 103 tests green either way.

The equivalent survivors N04 (`logoutHandoffs.clear()`), F03 (`<=` in place of `===`), N06 (no fallback to the spent RT) and A01 (fill only the oldest handoff) still survive. The fixer argues N04/F03 are equivalent 'in every reachable schedule' from the api.ts singleton. That holds only if the epoch is captured before the SecureStore read. Under the read-straddle, a refresh's epochAtRequest can equal a SECOND tap's pre-bump epoch, and N04 then lets the first logout's finally wipe the second logout's matching handoff. I did not reproduce this; it follows from the same trace as the straddle defect.
